title: Demineralization Plant
model_title: Demineralization Plant (Strong-Acid Cation → Degasser → Strong-Base Anion)

introduction.definition: A two-bed demineralization (DM) plant removes dissolved salts by ion exchange. A strong-acid cation exchanger replaces Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺ and Na⁺ with H⁺; a degasser blows out the CO₂ formed from bicarbonate; a strong-base anion exchanger replaces Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻ and silica with OH⁻. H⁺ and OH⁻ combine to water, giving low-conductivity water for boilers and processes.
applications: Boiler feed make-up for medium/high-pressure boilers
Process water for chemicals, pharmaceuticals and power

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Outlet conductivity vs throughput — flat then rising at exhaustion.

pressure.title: Ion exchange swaps salts for H⁺ and OH⁻
pressure.description: The cation resin exchanges Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺ for H⁺ (water becomes acidic); the degasser blows out the CO₂ formed from bicarbonate; the anion resin exchanges Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻, silica for OH⁻; H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O. Resins are regenerated with acid and caustic when exhausted (rising conductivity/silica or sodium slip). Typical outlet < 5–10 µS/cm, silica < ~ 0.1 mg/L.

foundation: Vessels on level foundation or legs anchored; space above for resin loading and below for underdrain access.
alignment: Vessels plumb so the bed and distributors are level (uneven beds channel).
piping: Valve nest with service, backwash, regenerant, rinse; sample points before/after; acid/caustic-resistant lines and safety showers.
commissioning: Load support layers and resin (soaked), backwash to classify; first regeneration; rinse to quality; check conductivity/silica/hardness.

lubrication: No routine lubrication on static parts; lubricate valve stems and actuators per maker.

causes: Anion exhausted, warm caustic not used

safety: Acid and caustic: PPE, safety showers, bunded storage; hydrogen release from some regenerations — ventilate.

script.narration: This module introduces the Demineralization Plant.
A two-bed demineralization (DM) plant removes dissolved salts by ion exchange.
A strong-acid cation exchanger replaces Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺ and Na⁺ with H⁺; a degasser blows out the CO₂ formed from bicarbonate; a strong-base anion exchanger replaces Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻ and silica with OH⁻.

script.narration: How the Demineralization Plant works.
Filtered water enters the cation exchanger.
Cation resin captures metal ions and releases H⁺.
The degasser strips CO₂.
The anion resin captures anions and releases OH⁻.
Acid and caustic regenerate the beds when exhausted.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Demineralization Plant — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Demineralization Plant.
Log throughput, conductivity and silica.
Resin sample and capacity test.
Inspect laterals/distributors; top up resin.
Watch for early exhaustion: short runs. Common cause: resin fouling.
Watch for silica slip: high silica. Common cause: anion exhausted, warm caustic not used.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
